chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd and Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the ghusl of the deceased, and he said: “Wash him with water and lote leaves, then after that wash him a second washing with water and camphor and dharīrah, if it is available, and wash him the third time with pure water: three washings.” I said: His entire body? He said: “Yes.” I said: Should there be a garment on him when he is washed? He said: “If you are able, let there be a shirt upon him, and wash him from beneath it.” And he said: “I prefer that the one who washes the deceased wrap a cloth around his hand until he washes him.”

key_terms.الْخِرْقَةَ: a cloth wrapped around the washer’s hand
key_terms.ذَرِيرَةٍ: a fragrant substance added if available during the washing
key_terms.سِدْرٍ: lote leaves used in the first washing of the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased before burial
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ: a shirt placed on the deceased while washing if possible
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor used in the second washing
key_terms.مَاءٍ قَرَاحٍ: pure unmixed water used in the final washing

ai.seo_question: How should the ghusl of the deceased be performed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the method of ghusl for the deceased: three washings, first with water and lote leaves, second with water and camphor and dharīrah if available, and third with pure water. It also states that the entire body is to be washed, that it is preferable for the deceased to have a shirt on during washing if possible, and that the washer should wrap a cloth around his hand.
